title: The House of God
note:
Primary, Chapter 2, from the Mar Thoma Sunday School Samajam Primary Vol-1, pages 13–15. The boy Jesus left behind in Jerusalem, told as a chapter about the Church being the House of God.

Memory verse and five-stage practice from the Memory Verse agent; see the verse note.

Games from the Game Builder agent (`npm run agent:games -- --class primary --chapter 02`). Its first run mis-read question 3 — “What did the parents *see*…” was filed as a process and handed a sequence, which would have asked a child to put a single glimpse into order — and could not read question 4 at all. The classifier now separates what somebody saw from what somebody did, and reads a quoted reply as its own shape; the second run planned reveal, multiple-choice, match and a choice for the reply. One mechanic was changed by hand after that and the reason is in that game’s note.

The page also carries the teacher’s Qurbana vocabulary in the margins — Thurible, Qurbana, Madbaha, Dhoopakutty — which belongs to the class rather than to any question. It is recorded in the curriculum note and used nowhere.

Question 4’s last word is cut off by the edge of the photograph. See the curriculum note.

No artwork: `04 - Story Artwork` for this chapter is empty in Drive, so the story is twenty-two text cards and no game carries a picture. The book’s colouring page also sets an activity — “Make a list of words that are related to Church” — which is a pencil-and-paper task for the class and has no game here.

story.text: Little Jesus was loved by his relatives and neighbours.
story.note:
No artwork exists for this chapter yet — `04 - Story Artwork` in Drive is empty, so every card here is words only and every `picture` names a panel nobody has drawn. The names follow the ordinary convention so `npm run art:fetch -- --from-dir` can drop the panels in with nothing here to edit.

Treat the card list as provisional. Beginner Chapter 5, Beginner Chapter 6 and Primary Chapter 3 were all written from the lesson alone and all three were rewritten when the artwork arrived carrying a shape the text did not have. If that happens again, the panels win.

story.text: He went to worship God regularly with his parents and relatives.
Every year His parents went to Jerusalem for the Festival of the Passover.
They walked together with friends and relatives for many days. It was a joyous journey.
When Jesus was twelve years old, they went to Jerusalem as usual.
After the festival, His parents set out for home.
But the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem.
His parents did not know. They thought He was with their relatives.
They travelled for a whole day before they began looking for Him.
They looked among their relatives and friends, and did not find Him.
So they went back to Jerusalem to look for Him.
After three days they found Him in the temple courts.
He was sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions.
His mother said, “Son, why have you treated us like this?”
“Your father and I have been anxiously searching for you.”
He asked her, “Why were you searching for me?”
“Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?”
When they heard this, they did not say anything.
Then Jesus went down to Nazareth and grew up in obedience to them.
The Church is the House of God, our Father.
Jesus teaches us to go to church and take part in all it does.
Even as we follow God, we should also obey our earthly parents.

curriculum.source: Primary Mar Thoma Vol-1, Chapter 02 “THE HOUSE OF GOD”, p.14 — “ANSWER THE QUESTIONS”
curriculum.note:
The four questions the Primary book prints under the lesson on p.14, transcribed from the curriculum photographs in 01 - Curriculum Source.

The page carries the teacher’s own answer key in pen, ① to ④, and each `answer` below is the sentence its mark points at, quoted from p.14 rather than reasoned out. The same page carries a second set of handwritten notes in the margins — Thurible, Qurbana, Madbaha, Dhoopakutty and their meanings — which are the teacher’s own Qurbana vocabulary for the class and belong to no question here. They are recorded in this note and nowhere else.

**Question 4’s last word is cut off by the edge of the photograph.** The line reads “What was Jesus’ reply when His parents asked Him about making them anxio…” and the page edge falls there. It is written out as “anxious” below, which is the only word that fits and matches the mother’s own “anxiously searching” three lines above — but it is a completion, not a reading, and a re-photograph of p.14 with its right margin would settle it.

questions.question: Why were Jesus’ parents unaware of His absence on their return journey?
questions.objective: They assumed He was with their relatives, and travelled a whole day before they began looking.
questions.answer: “But His parents did not know about it. Thinking that He was with his relatives, they travelled for a day.” (p.14)

questions.question: Where did the parents go in search of Jesus who was missing?
questions.objective: Back to Jerusalem — after looking among their relatives and friends and not finding Him.
questions.answer: “Then they began looking for Him among their relatives and friends. Since they did not find Him, they went back to Jerusalem to look for Him.” (p.14)

questions.question: What did the parents see when they found Jesus?
questions.objective: Jesus in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
questions.answer: “After three days they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions.” (p.14)

questions.question: What was Jesus’ reply when His parents asked Him about making them anxious?
questions.objective: “Why were you searching for me? Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?”
questions.answer: “He asked her, ‘Why were you searching for me? Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?’” (p.14)
questions.note: Marked ④ on the page. The question’s last word is cut off by the photograph’s edge — see the block note.

games.title: Why They Did Not Know
games.objective: Hold the whole of the lesson's answer: they assumed He was with their relatives, and a full day passed before they looked.
games.note: Question 1. A reveal, because the lesson gives the answer as a small chain rather than one fact — a crowd of relatives, an assumption, a day’s walking, and only then a search. A quiz would make a child pick one link and call the rest wrong.

items.label: They travelled in a big group
They thought He was with relatives

games.title: Where They Looked
games.objective: Name Jerusalem — where they went back to, after the people around them turned out not to have Him.
games.note: Question 2. Two of the wrong options are the places they had already been — among their relatives, and on the road home — so a child who remembers the searching but not its ending has somewhere to go wrong. Nazareth is where the chapter ends rather than where they searched.

interactions.prompt: Where did they go to look for Jesus?
interactions.hint: They turned round and went back.

games.title: What They Found
games.objective: Picture the scene the lesson describes — where He was, who He was with, and the two things He was doing.
games.note: Question 3. The lesson answers it with one scene that has four things in it at once, so the game pairs each thing with what it was — the place, the company, and both halves of what He was doing. The planner first read this question as a *process* and offered a sequence, which would have asked a child to put a single glimpse into order; the classifier now separates what somebody saw from what somebody did, and this is the question that taught it.

interactions.prompt: Match each one to what it was.
interactions.hint: He was doing two things, not one.

games.title: What Jesus Said
games.objective: Name what Jesus said He had to be doing — the answer He gave His parents instead of an apology.
games.note:
Question 4, and the mechanic changed twice. The planner offered a multiple-choice; it was overridden to `arrange-words`, which is what the preference table lists first for a quotation and much closer to saying a sentence out loud than picking it off a list — and then it was changed back, because this chapter’s memory verse turned out to be that exact sentence. St. Luke 2: 49 *is* Jesus’ reply, and the verse practice rebuilds it twice, at four pieces and at six. A game that rebuilt it a third time would be the same task wearing a different name.

So the game asks what the reply *said* and the practice handles its words. The third wrong option is what His parents had assumed, and the fourth is the apology He did not give. Four options is the Primary band’s ceiling.

Worth remembering when planning: the verse and the games have to be laid out together, because a chapter whose memory verse is a sentence from its own lesson can end up drilling it twice.

interactions.prompt: Jesus said He had to be where?
interactions.hint: He answered their question with a question.

celebration.message: Jesus loved His Father’s house. You can love it too.
celebration.note: The lesson’s own application — the Church is the House of God — said back to the child.

verse.text: “Why were you searching for me?” he asked. “Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?”

practice.hint: He answered their question with a question.
words: “Didn’t you know I had to be
practice.note: Stage 1, phrase ordering, cut by hand rather than by the agent. Its Primary rung cut this verse at even word counts and produced “for me?” he asked. “Didn’t” — a piece that begins in the middle of one quotation and ends in the middle of the next, with the quotation marks split across the join. A verse with speech in it needs cutting at the speech, so these four pieces break where the quotation marks do. The build checks they spell the verse exactly.

practice.prompt: “Why were you ______ for me?” he asked.
practice.hint: It is what His parents had been doing for three days.
practice.note: Stage 2, the missing word with the sentence whole around it. Four options, all real words of this verse.

practice.prompt: he asked. “Didn’t you know I had to be in my ______
practice.hint: Whose house did Jesus call it?
practice.note: Stage 3, the right-hand side taken away. The word is the point of the whole verse — He called the temple His Father’s house — so it is the one worth supplying from memory rather than reading around.

practice.hint: Two questions, and three words between them.
practice.note: Stage 4, full reconstruction — six pieces where stage 1 had four. Each quotation mark still travels with the words it belongs to.

practice.prompt: Where does our verse come from?
practice.hint: It is inside this chapter's own Bible portion.
practice.note: Stage 5, the reference. All three are inside this chapter’s own portion, St. Luke 2: 41 - 52, printed on p.13 — 41 is where it begins and 52 is where it ends. A child who has read the chapter has met all three, which is what makes choosing between them a question rather than a guess.

verse.note:
Read from the chapter’s last page through the Memory Verse agent: `--fetch --source-dir` over the curriculum photographs, the supervised read, then `--from-extraction`. That page lives in `06 - Memory Verse` rather than in `01 - Curriculum Source`, which is why this chapter first shipped without a verse at all — the agent was pointed at the wrong folder, not at a gap.

Five stages in the shape Primary Chapter 3 uses: phrase ordering, a gap with the sentence whole on both sides of it, the same gap with the right-hand side taken away, a finer reconstruction, and the reference chosen against near misses. Translation is unresolved: the page does not name one, which is where every chapter in this library stands.

This verse is Jesus’ own reply, which is also what question 4 of this chapter asks about — so the fourth game was changed to ask what the reply *said* rather than rebuild its words a third time. See that game’s note.

Printed with curly quotation marks around both halves of the speech and “he asked.” between them; all of it is kept, and every arrangement above spells it exactly.

decision.statement: The Church is the House of God. I will go to church and participate in the worship.
decision.note: The curriculum’s own My Decision line from p.16, unchanged.

song.note: The Song from p.16, in the Latin script the book prints it in, line for line.

prayer.text: Loving Father, train me to go to church regularly. Amen.
prayer.note: The closing Prayer from p.16, word for word. The chapter also opens with a prayer on p.13 — “Jesus, help us to understand about Your visit to the house of God in Your childhood. Amen.” — which is recorded here rather than lost.
